model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between ACC (%) and the Co-occurrence Number, displaying six distinct methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME. The x-axis represents the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 0 to 10^3, with tick marks at intervals of 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale, ranging from 40 to 65, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The Base method is shown as a black line with solid markers, starting at approximately 39% ACC at a Co-occurrence Number of 0 and rising to about 44% at 1000. The MEND method is depicted as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at approximately 44% ACC and increasing to about 57% at 1000. The FT method is a blue line with triangle markers, starting at approximately 40% ACC and rising to about 48% at 1000. The MEMIT method is a purple line with circle markers, starting at approximately 44% ACC and increasing to about 55% at 1000. The IKE method is a red line with triangle markers, beginning at approximately 43% ACC and increasing to about 50% at 1000. The ROME method is a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 51% ACC and increasing to about 66% at 1000.
